text:
mira: Heads-up — onboarding run for the sampleapp is failing for org-scoped keys. Repro steps: set REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT=acme:payments then run `./start`. Error says `invalid scope`.
alex: Can you paste the exact error and env vars (redact keys)?
mira: Error log:
```
2024-03-12T14:02:09Z ERROR auth failed status=403 msg=\"invalid scope: project not allowed\"
request: POST /v1/generate
headers: authorization: REDACTED
```
Env vars: `REDWOOD_API_KEY=***`, `REDWOOD_PROJECT=acme:payments`, no `REDWOOD_KEY` set.
jordan: This smells like the CLI/SDK env var mismatch. Historically the CLI looked for `REDWOOD_KEY` and the SDK reads `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. If sampleapp shells out to the CLI for some calls it can end up with different auth behavior.
sam: Also worth noting: when a key is org-scoped (org:project), the auth service expects an explicit `x-redwood-project` header for non-default project usage. If the SDK didn't inject that header (because it only sees `REDWOOD_API_KEY`), the backend rejects.
mira: Hmm — sampleapp is a tiny mix of direct SDK calls and a helper script that uses the CLI. So yep, mix-and-match.
alex: Short-term workaround: set `REDWOOD_KEY` to the same value as `REDWOOD_API_KEY` and export `REDWOOD_PROJECT` — that'll make both code paths consistent.
alex: Medium-term fix: unify precedence in the sampleapp and upstream SDK to prefer `REDWOOD_API_KEY` and have the CLI honor that env var. Add clear docs about project header injection.
jordan: Proposed code snippet for precedence (from memory):
```js
// pseudo-env precedence
const key = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY || process.env.REDWOOD_KEY || readFromConfig();
const project = process.env.REDWOOD_PROJECT || process.env.REDWOOD_DEFAULT_PROJECT;
// inject header if project is present and key is org-scoped
if (project && key.includes(':')) req.headers['x-redwood-project'] = project;
```
sam: Another edge: key rotation. When users rotate via console, the CLI daemon caches tokens in `~/.cache/redwood` for long requests. If sampleapp relied on cached token it won't see the rotated value until cache expires. We should surface a CLI flag `--no-cache` or a quick invalidation on rotate.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: sampleapp-staging deploy succeeded at 2024-03-12T14:05:00Z :rocket:
mira: I can make a small patch to the sampleapp to standardize env var usage and add a README blurb. Want me to also open an issue against the SDK to ensure header injection for project-scoped keys?
alex: Yes please — open a small issue and link the sampleapp PR. Make the PR change explicit: 1) use `REDWOOD_API_KEY` everywhere; 2) set `REDWOOD_KEY` fallback during transition; 3) add integration test that uses an org:project key and asserts the `x-redwood-project` header.
sam: I'll take the SDK issue. I'll add a unit test and a note in the CLI about honoring `REDWOOD_API_KEY` too so we don't drift.
jordan: Can we also add a dev onboarding checklist: "If onboarding fails with 403, confirm env var parity and try `export REDWOOD_KEY=$REDWOOD_API_KEY` and `--no-cache` for the CLI" — small but would save a bunch of pings.
mira: Awesome. Thanks all. I'll push the sampleapp PR in ~30m and tag @alex for review. :thumbsup:
